Q078-04.notes: -10 <= -2x < 4 -> 5 >= x > -2 -> -2 < x <= 5. B is the unflipped-endpoint trap, C the complement.

Q078-06.notes: -2(x-3) = -2x+6, not -6; Step 1 wrong. Steps 2-4 follow correctly from Step 1. Correct solution x=0.

Q078-07.notes: x-int -3, y-int b: area (1/2)(3)|b|=12 -> |b|=8; slope = b/3 negative -> b=-8, slope -8/3 (also -2.666/-2.667 accepted). Negative-slope condition correctly makes the answer unique.

Q078-09.notes: Both = 0.4*30% = 12% of school = 25% of choir -> choir = 48%. Distractors 12 (both), 18.75 (30*0.25/0.4), 70 (100-30) plausible.

flags: minor: quartile convention not stated; conclusion robust under standard conventions
Q078-10.notes: D: A has >=20 scores <=75 (20th value <=75); B has at most 10 <=75 (11th value >=80). Must hold. Counterexamples: A mean undetermined (skew A high / B low). B: A could have 10 >=86 (30th=82,31st..40th>=86) vs B 5 (15th=85,16th=87) -> false. C: A could have exactly 10 >=80 (21st-30th in 75-79) vs B 11 (10th=11th=80) -> false. Built both.

Q078-11.notes: Per 100 households people: 25+70+60+60+25=240; in 4+ households 60+25=85; 85/240=17/48. Trap A (household proportion 20%). D 17/20 (85/100) also a trap. Requires person-weighting insight.

Q078-12.notes: Confounder: sicker patients transferred to ICU-heavy hospitals.

Q078-13.notes: 30%/10 = 3%; 3%/5 = 0.6%. Trap: dividing by 9 and 4 instead of 10 and 5.
